review_text:
I bought this laptop in 2016 and it arrived near the start of January, currently I am writing about this near the start of February 2020. I would say that in the beginning I bought this for gaming mainly LoL, watching movies and doing homework. The battery life was wonderful compared to my old HP laptop especially if I was just browsing the web or typing an essay. I would get about 6-8hrs. I ended up using this laptop less and less throughout the years. I mainly used it for schoolwork that requires using a computer such as online essays, classes or using certain computer programs. As of now there has been times when the sound gives a screech whenever a video or music is playing. There also been blue screens for crash dumps and the laptop needed to restart. I can't watch an hour long video for an assignment and still have enough battery power to type an essay after that. This also occurs with windows or some security updates as well. And this is with the battery power saver always on. Of course battery life do degrade over time so does every other electrical device. But I thought it would have lasted a bit longer due to my minimal usage. I would be lucky to get over 2hrs of battery power for me to work on stuff on campus. Sometimes the battery power would say I have 2hrs and 47 minutes of battery power left at 80% but when it hits 78% I suddenly only have 2hrs left. Lately I've been contemplating over whether or not I should even bring my laptop to school if I can't get most of work done on it and have to search for a free computer available during my gap between classes.
I do like that the fans on this laptop works so much better than my HP laptop. So it isn't as noisy or if it does use the fans it will only last a couple of seconds and then becomes silent again. I mean overall this laptop beats the HP infinity I had before since that laptop literally heated up so bad that the mother board got burnt and it wouldn't turn on after 4 years. At least after 4 years with this laptop I still have a usable laptop that is still speedy like when I first got it. But the battery doesn't last as long as I would've liked. And this laptop doesn't have an easily removable battery either. Well back to my online assignment. :c

review_text:
Light weight and portable laptop. Build quality is good overall but screen seems delicate. Integrated battery claims 9 hr life but more realistic expectation is about 5 at mid-high brightness. Plenty of USB ports, including USB C. You can charge thru USB C but it took longer in my experience.

8 GB RAM is not a lot but it does handle heavy CPU loads well. I have read that RAM is expandable on this model but I haven't installed more at time of writing. It will run small files on Solidworks or Excel easily but will stutter with large files as expected. Movie playback is smooth on main monitor and external monitor with/without desktop stretching. The fan runs a lot and will be audible in quiet spaces such as a library but is not disruptive. I hate the offset trackpad but others might not. Keyboard backlight has 3 settings (off, medium, max).

Speakers sound good but have no low end. Loud if desired. I recommend uninstalling FusionTech's proprietary audio software and indeed all of the FusionTech bloatware except for FusionTech updater. On a related note, it ran a BIOS update after about 20 hours of use so hopefully that was normal because otherwise it's unsettling.

I have not had any hardware or OS issues. On low quality, GTAV averages mid-upper 30's fps steady. Maxed out, Overwatch averages upper 40's fps with occasional dips to 30's. Lagspikes on all games if you use Gamebar. Keyboard response is good for gaming, not mushy at least for now.

Its too bad because the build and components were solid for the price besides the hinge issue. FusionTech should not have skimped on the hinges because that is a crucial function of the laptop, and should last more than 2 years.

I ended up buying another FusionTech but made sure to get a model with metal hinges this time.

review_text:
I bought this laptop open box for around $970, definitely not cheap, but a steal for this particular laptop.
The build quality is top notch, screen nice and bright, and just feeling the carbon fiber palm rest is treat by itself.
After the first impressions wore off then came all the problems.
When I reached my car after buying the laptop I opened up the lid to just make sure everything was in order. I put the laptop back in the box and when I got home i discovered that the laptop had been running the whole ride home with the lid closed and was SO SO HOT I COULDN'T EVEN TOUCH IT WITHOUT BURNING MYSELF. It was actually terrifyingly hot. I put the case under my room fan at full speed to cool it down.
Next problem. After using it for about 20 minutes, I found my screen would continuously turn off while I was using it! Like completely turn off as if I was putting it to sleep. After about 8 hours of stress and troubleshooting and countless hours with FusionTech support (to their credit they were very helpful) FusionTech support tells me that there is a setting called "panel self refresh" in the Intel graphics settings that was causing the display to malfunction, and turning the display off. Problem fixed.
NEXT. The thermals. OH THE THERMALS. They are BAD For the processor specifically. It is a very powerful processor. But at stock settings, even opening a few programs at the same time would shoot the processor up to 100 degrees C, making the fans shoot up to maximum speed (quite loud), and the it would thermal throttle relentlessly. I ended up undervolting my processor using a program called throttle stop, and the thermals are better, but this is not something I think the average consumer should have to do to make sure their laptop isn't thermal throttling into oblivion. The GPU (GTX 1650) stays relatively cool (72 C), even under heavy load. No complaints there.
NEXT PROBLEM. The display. There are other versions with IPS panels. I ended up with OLED panel version. It's bright. It's gorgeous. It's 4k. It's almost bezelless. BUT (another BUT), it has noticeable banding with a full grey screen at all brightness levels. It's kinda annoying.
After much research into the problem, I found this OLED panel (made by Samsung) is used in many other pretty high end laptops, and is a widespread issue for all of them. A quick google search for "OLED Banding" confirmed this. The version with the IPS panel does not suffer from this issue.
If you can find this laptop for decent price, sure, it's got some serious value. I wouldn't buy it anywhere near its retail price. Considering the price I got it at ($970), I don't think I'll return it. I'm very savvy with tech and found my way around the issues I've found, other than the OLED panel banding, which is an issue I think I'll live with, but I feel bad for the people who spent full retail price for it and have to deal with the said issues pointed out in my review

review_text:
I bought this laptop open box for around $970, definitely not cheap, but a steal for this particular laptop.
The build quality is top notch, screen nice and bright, and just feeling the carbon fiber palm rest is treat by itself.
After the first impressions wore off then came all the problems.
When I reached my car after buying the laptop I opened up the lid to just make sure everything was in order. I put the laptop back in the box and when I got home i discovered that the laptop had been running the whole ride home with the lid closed and was SO SO HOT I COULDN'T EVEN TOUCH IT WITHOUT BURNING MYSELF. It was actually terrifyingly hot. I put the case under my room fan at full speed to cool it down.
Next problem. After using it for about 20 minutes, I found my screen would continuously turn off while I was using it! Like completely turn off as if I was putting it to sleep. After about 8 hours of stress and troubleshooting and countless hours with FusionTech support (to their credit they were very helpful) FusionTech support tells me that there is a setting called "panel self refresh" in the Intel graphics settings that was causing the display to malfunction, and turning the display off. Problem fixed.
NEXT. The thermals. OH THE THERMALS. They are BAD For the processor specifically. It is a very powerful processor. But at stock settings, even opening a few programs at the same time would shoot the processor up to 100 degrees C, making the fans shoot up to maximum speed (quite loud), and the it would thermal throttle relentlessly. I ended up undervolting my processor using a program called throttle stop, and the thermals are better, but this is not something I think the average consumer should have to do to make sure their laptop isn't thermal throttling into oblivion. The GPU (GTX 1650) stays relatively cool (72 C), even under heavy load. No complaints there.
NEXT PROBLEM. The display. There are other versions with IPS panels. I ended up with OLED panel version. It's bright. It's gorgeous. It's 4k. It's almost bezelless. BUT (another BUT), it has noticeable banding with a full grey screen at all brightness levels. It's kinda annoying.
After much research into the problem, I found this OLED panel (made by Samsung) is used in many other pretty high end laptops, and is a widespread issue for all of them. A quick google search for "OLED Banding" confirmed this. It's not just a problem for this laptop either, OLED TV's have this issue as well, so it seems like this is an issue I will just have to live with. The version with the IPS panel does not suffer from this issue.
If you can find this laptop for decent price, sure, it's got some serious value. I wouldn't buy it anywhere near its retail price. Considering the price I got it at ($970), I don't think I'll return it. I'm very savvy with tech and found my way around the issues I've found, other than the OLED panel banding, which is an issue I think I'll live with, but I feel bad for the people who spent full retail price for it and have to deal with the said issues pointed out in my review

product_name: FusionTech Worktop 15 7000, 15.6” FHD Display, 9th Gen Intel Core i7-9750H, NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1050, 256 SSD HD, 8GB RAM (i7590-7865BLK-PUS)
review_text:
I bought this laptop to use primarily for music production, web design / coding, light gaming (mostly steam), and, of course, general-purpose use. I also bought the laptop knowing that the memory and SSD were not sufficient for my needs, with the intent of upgrading these components. My review is written from this perspective, so the value or importance I place on certain features won't necessarily be relevant to everyone. With that said, I do feel this is an all-around good laptop that can successfully fill many roles.

The process of adding additional RAM and upgrading the SSD was easy, and after doing so, I am more than satisfied with the performance of this laptop and still managed to spend (barely) less than $1,000 total. I've also benchmarked it against other laptops at or near the $1000 price point and it consistently out performs the competition. I've decided to break my review into three sections: good, neutral, and bad to discuss the things I really like about it, the things I'm indifferent about, and the things I don't really like. Here we go:

Good:

CPU - no doubt the star of this laptop, the intel i7-9750h is a 6-core, 12-thread 2.6ghz base clock, 4.5ghz turbo workhorse of a laptop processor. It actually out-performs the newer i7-1065g7 and i7-10510u 10th gen CPUs that are commonly found in the newest laptops.

Dedicated GPU - the nvidia GTX 1050 graphics card really does perform quite well for a laptop that is not branded as a gaming laptop, I consistently get around 85 FPS. It also has 3GB of dedicated GDDR5.

IPS Screen - I have a couple of nags about the screen under the neutral section, but the IPS screen does produce a vibrant, crisp picture and the thin bezel is quite nice.

Light-weight - at first I wasn't completely sold on the magnesium alloy design because it felt more like plastic when compared to my previous aluminum laptop, but it quickly grew on me. It is very light weight, yet doesn't feel flimsy. Overall the built quality of this laptop is good.

USB-C charging - this is really nice to have and a nice step forward in standardizing laptop charging.

Back-lit keyboard - I often use my laptop in low-light environments so this is a must for me.

10-key number pad - this is nice to have and honestly impressive that they managed to include this on a smaller 15.6" design.

Neutral:

Battery life is around 4 - 5 hours. Not great, but not bad considering it's a 3-cell, 56wh battery driving a 6-core i7 and a GTX 1050. The battery can be upgraded to a 6-cell, 97wh battery, so that's worth consideration.

Memory - it comes with 8GB of DDR4 RAM, which is not bad, but not great by today's standards, fortunately, it's in a single module with a secondary, unoccupied slot, so buying and installing an additional RAM module is easy.

SSD - The SSD in this laptop is not great by today's standards either. It's not terrible, but 256gb is a bit small and the read / write speeds are nothing amazing. Of course, the importance of this completely depends on your use case. For example, I store a lot of data in cloud storage, so massive capacity is not that important to me. I also purchased the laptop with the intent to replace the SSD.

No touch screen - most modern FusionTech laptops have touch screen, but this one does not.

Screen resolution - this is kind of nitpicking, but it would be nice if this laptop supported higher screen resolutions on the internal display. The GTX 1050 is capable of outputting 4K (and greater).

Touchpad - could be bigger and smoother, but it works well enough and has all the expected multi-touch features. I use a wireless mouse most of the time so I don't really care about the touchpad.

Bad:

No Ethernet port - I work as a network technician and often have to plug network cables into my laptop to test and troubleshoot. I have a USB-C to Ethernet adapter that works fine with the laptop, but it's just a pain to have to remember to carry it around when I need it.

Cooling / Thermal - The laptop can get very hot during extended periods of performance-heavy use.

I’m not even going to get into the issues with the wrong description of this laptop, and I’m not taking that into consideration at all because I think that is an amazon mess up and not FusionTech. But I do want to quickly comment on the many reviews about receiving used FusionTech laptops because they had a FusionTech return label on them. As I said before this is now my 4th FusionTech laptop in the last I believe 12 years and they have all had that FusionTech label on them. It’s not a return label. I have had no problems with overheating l, though I mostly use this for work and a few other smaller activities so nothing like gaming or anything like that.

Overall I wish I could say I love this laptop, but I can’t. I like it, and it works great for most of what I need it for, besides zoom meetings due to the camera quality. Is it perfect? Nope. But it’s overall a pretty solid laptop and it works.

The laptop worked great until I called FusionTech, they dialed in and performed a diagnostics on the system. There was a memory card error. Sent the laptop to FusionTech. Then it was a motherboard issue. Escalated and found out the errors were because the seller installed unsupported third-party components and components that were beyond the motherboard's ability to support.

The seller used third-party parts for the memory cards (16G each) and replaced the 128G SSD with a 512G SSD. FusionTech's motherboard for this laptop only supports 8G memory cards and 128G SSD. In addition, the board does not support third-party components and will generate error codes.

FusionTech explained these issues void the warranty. Contacted the seller and sent me a legal quote from Mag-Moss Warranty Act stating why FusionTech can't refuse my warranty. The issue is the seller modified the laptop beyond its supportability. FusionTech offers a laptop with this config that is supported but the seller opted to modify a lower-end laptop and sell it as a higher-end laptop.

The point is the seller is deceptive in the product presentation and the issues can cause malfunctions with the laptop that FusionTech will not cover or fix. I wouldn't have found this out if I had not happened to run a health diagnostic from FusionTech on the laptop.

review_text:
It's taken me a week or so to fully digest the functionality and pros/cons of this laptop. Overall, if you read the product description (and know anything about electronics) it's pretty straight forward what you're getting. That being said, I feel it's important to outline a few cool features as well as drawbacks you may overlook.

Initial Impression: Materially, this is a really solid piece of equipment. Though somewhat heavier than I expected, this is typical with a gaming laptop. The power adapter is massive however, and unnecessarily so. I don't know if this has anything to do with requiring more energy for intense gaming, but it's literally a quarter the size of the laptop itself. The keys are backlit (which can be turned on and off with the press of a button), and there are ports for virtually everything you could imagine. The screen itself is somewhat of a matte texture which is something I'm not used to, but after a few hours of use I appreciated how it prevents glare. As with most laptops, the brightness is adjustable on the keyboard - something to take into consideration when trying to preserve battery life. That being said, startup was a nightmare... but this was due largely in part to my internet being down - an essential requirement to get up and running. I'm very much a "plug and play" kind of guy, so you can imagine my frustration when the computer repeatedly froze on a black screen until I was able to get online to download essential updates and software components (all of which should be pre-installed for a device this new). Trying to add a secondary user was equally frustrating as it also needed to re-download many of the same components as my setup, once again freezing repeatedly. Once past all the initial turmoil, everything was a breeze.

Extended use: After a full charge, the battery lasted roughly 2.5-3 hours while I browsed the internet and worked on documents. With streaming and game play, the battery life is surprisingly close to the same (roughly 2 hours depending how much multi-tasking you're doing). The dual fan system is incredibly quiet and kept the laptop from heating more than say your average smartphone after prolonged use.

Cortana is your virtual assistant (similar to Siri). While she is accessible from your desktop, you can also enable "Hey Cortana" in the settings which will allow her to respond to voice commands.

Link your phone using the edge app. This allows you to sync browsing history, favorites, and alternate seamlessly between devices (simply by logging into your Microsoft account). It is worth noting the functionality for Apple products is more limited than Android (which allows you to see/sync SMS, MMS, pictures, and video). I have an iPhone, so I cannot personally attest to whether or not the additional Android features actually work, but the information showed up while setting up my device.

Game Shift, a function controlled by a button on your keyboard, is said to increase the fan speed to cool the processor, and prioritizes game data over annoying popups or background apps (and updates). Basically, it is supposed to optimize the resources needed during gaming (processor, video card, memory, etc). I attempted to test this function with several games and did not notice a difference or receive the on-screen prompt that it was working. Perhaps I need to update a driver for this? It wouldn't surprise me given the number of essentials I had to install during setup. That being said, the gaming I did was pretty seamless and ran without issues.

It's worth mentioning there is no CD/DVD drive. I completely overlooked this prior to ordering, and the vast majority of my software is on discs. This is easily resolvable with an external drive which costs virtually nothing nowadays.

The webcam has an indicator light next to it to ensure privacy (so you know when it's on). The resolution is average, but consistent with other laptop cams on the market.

Lastly, a few quick notes. As an avid gamer and video editor, I will say one thing I found discouraging is the computer's memory. Though this is something easily resolved with an external drive, all of these "plug in" devices begin to defeat the purpose and simplicity of a laptop. Additionally, the included manual indicates a fingerprint reader on/by the power button... this is NOT a standard feature with all G3 models.

Summary: When utilized for office use (or basic functionality) this laptop is superior in terms of speed and software capabilities. For standard gaming it's average, and for the professional gamer it might be underwhelming in some of the areas outlined above. Still, when put to the test it's a reliable laptop that I'd consider a nice addition to FusionTech's product line.

review_text:
Just to be clear, as they have merged the reviews of several FusionTech laptop models; I am reviewing a FusionTech Worktop 15 7501 laptop which was first released in July 2020. It does not have an optical drive and is extremely light and thin for a laptop of this size.

I decided to review this from the standpoint of someone getting their first computer. I am somewhat suited for such a task, having not owned a PC since Windows 98. That said I was shocked by what a miserable experience it was trying to activate and operate this FusionTech Worktop 15 out of the box. Part of this is simply what happens when a Mac user encounters a PC. And part is more directed at Windows 10 than against the features of this specific PC model.

Judging from this, over the past 20+ years there has been little that I would regard as improvements made to entry level FusionTech laptops, while complexity has increased geometrically it seems to have been almost entirely in the service of showcasing silly gimmicks. It is certainly a more powerful machine than my 1998 PC, so the internet connection permits streaming and gaming applications; and apparently it can handle ZOOM but I have had it for over six weeks and am still getting nowhere trying to utilize this feature.

My 1998 PC out of the box had an optical drive and the installed software to run Excel and Word. And with a simple driver could link to and operate a printer and a scanner. Navigation could be figured out in a couple of hours.

But out of the box with this 2020 version I have been limited to accessing the internet and to sending and receiving email. That has been the sum total of its functionality. Although based on Amazon's product detail page there are all sorts of bells and whistles designed into this machine. To be fair, with my basic computer needs I suspect that even if I could figure out how to activate them they would be of little value. I really wish the designers of these basic machines would spend less time trying to dazzle buyers with things that complicate their lives and come out with something that could simply be plugged and immediately applied to a useful purpose.

Within hours of opening the box I was wishing that I had not attempted to use it as there were so many invasive questions asked during the registration and set-up that I expect to be plagued with thousands of spam emails over the next decade. I think that I switched off most of the “receive offers” options and hopefully avoided disclosing my telephone number but I regret ever opening up this can of worms. I had my first unwanted email within minutes of disclosing my address.

What you get in the box is the laptop itself and a power cord (no mouse although that is a quick enough fix). There are also two small brochures with microscopic print regarding warranty information and several tiny diagrams with minimal explanation. When you turn it on they begin extracting personal information and internet connection details. The operation of the laptop and the operating system are not intuitive so if you are not an experienced PC user make sure you have someone handy who can help you navigate the operation of this device. The screen is pretty much blank and there are few hints about where to find files or downloads. Portable hard drives and optical drives are only acknowledged, reading them requires outside apps or guidance.

It took me 40 minutes just to figure out how to use their menu to enter my date of birth, it would not allow me to just type it in the field. It took about the same amount of time for Cortina (the chatty set-up assistant) and I to give up on activating the fingerprint reader; she simply stopped prompting me and I thought it was finally activated - but the next time I tried to log-on it did not work. I was able to access the internet and I eventually I stumbled across the Microsoft Office software. But the software requires yet another registration and is only good for seven days before you have to purchase a subscription; seriously can't FusionTech just provide generic pre-installed software for something this basic?

To be fair there are online courses and books that will allow you to track up the learning curve and there is always on-line tech support if you want to devote even more hours to the task.

First impression is that this is a flimsy feeling laptop, with moderate effort you could fold the screen in half. Overall a huge disappointment for me but a seasoned Windows 10 user will not experience the same setup irritations.

product_name: FusionTech Worktop 15 5000 5577 Gaming Laptop - (15.6" Full HD (1920x1080), Intel Quad-Core i5-7300HQ Processor, 1TB HDD, 8GB DDR4 DRAM, NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1050 4GB VRAM, Windows 10
review_text:
So, my partner bought this laptop for me back in late 2017 (which is why you won't see a verified purchase for me; it's on their Amazon account). A few months into buying it, I had issues with the internal power supply, so I ended up having to send it to FusionTech to get it repaired (it was still in warranty). Since then, it's been absurdly stable, and the only real issue I've had is that the screen appears to occasionally flicker oddly and become all washed out.

I've upgraded the stock HDD to dual SSDs (one NVMe, one SATA), upgraded the RAM to 16 GB (2x8GB, using the stock + an extra 8GB), and currently run Ubuntu 20.04 LTS as my sole OS. Even at stock components, the computer is snappy and performs well, assuming you tweak the OS to fit the computer. That's easier said than done, but I had a perfectly tweaked stock Win10 + WSL setup, Debian setup, Manjaro setup, and Ubuntu setup on this thing.

If you buy this computer new from FusionTech, do yourself a favor and either do a Fresh Start in Windows 10 or wipe the hard drive and start with a stock OS. This will get rid of all the FusionTech garbage and give you stock settings and open up some settings that are locked down in the FusionTech-modified version of Win10. You *will* have to download nvidia's drivers, but Windows 10 should boot in Intel mode by default. Ubuntu won't, but if you tweak GRUB settings (add nouveau.modeset="0" to the startup command line on installer boot and first boot), you'll get a booting system.

Once running, you'll want to do something about power limit throttling. The main issue with this laptop isn't heat (though heat is still sometimes an issue, if you can disassemble laptops it is never a bad idea to replace the internal cooling compound with something a bit fresher), it's the overzealous processor governor that drops the 4x2.5GHz (3.5GHz turbo) i5 to its minimum of 0.8GHz whenever the governor thinks the processor is drawing too much power. I forget exactly how to change it in Windows (it's been a while), but in Ubuntu, the solution turned out to be 'uninstall all processor governors and let the processor self-govern'.

After all this is done, what do you get? You get a relatively cheap laptop with a discrete graphics card. Performance is high even when running Windows games through the added overhead of WINE and Proton (which translates Windows/DirectX commands to Linux/Vulkan). I consistently get 60 FPS with max settings in Warframe pretty much everywhere except the open-world areas, where framerates sometimes drop to the low 50s. Moreover, it's snappy and responsive for everyday tasks, but again, only once you've fixed the power limit throttle slowdowns.

If you're fine with tweaking a laptop's default setup to better suit the hardware and looking up problems for obscure issues, this laptop will surprise you with just how much power is in it. If not, you'll be limited to some extent.

review_text:
This is a review of the FusionTech Worktop 15 5501 15.6 inch FHD Laptop (Silver) Intel Core i7-1065G7 10th Gen, 8GB DDR4 RAM, 512GB SSD, Nvidia Geforce MX330 2GB GDDR5, Windows 10 Home (i7501-7623SLV-PUS).

Let's start with the basics:

If you look at the picture with the System Info, you will see that I was delivered a laptop with an Intel i7-1065G7 CPU. The sales page states that this model should be equipped with an Intel 10750H, a new chip with different characteristics. The bottom line is that the old chip does use less power due to it's using 4 Cores, 8 Threads @1.30 GHz, at 15 W. The newer chip uses more power and thus drains the battery more quickly, but it is much faster using 6 Cores, 12 Threads @2.60 GHz, at 45 W.

Notice also on the picture that shows the Display Info for this machine, this unit came equipped with an NVIDIA GeForce MX330, while the sales page says Nvidia Geforce GTX 1650 4GB GDDR6. In this case, the MX330 is a newer, better chip than the GTX so, I was downgraded on the CPU and upgraded on the GPU (Graphics chip)

I think it evens out in that the faster display and more display memory probably offsets some of the lower computing power. I don't know for sure, I just know it's a different setup than I thought I was getting.

I posted the results of the third-party testing that I did in the photos. As you can see the CPU (remember, this is not what was advertised, it is a slower version) came with an average rating of 55th percentile, nothing to write home about but then again, good for general use with no issues whatever. Notice that the GPU rates in the 90th percentile. This is the chip that was newer and better than advertised. Overall, compared to a "budget laptop" this 3rd party test showed this running about 143% better than a typical budget computer. Specifically, the CPU was 133% higher and the GPU was 247% higher. Again, this correlates to the slower CPU installed and the faster Graphics chip installed. Now, I wouldn't call this a "budget" computer and maybe the comparison was unfair. The other option for comparison was "gaming computer" and that would have made this look bad but would have been a very poor comparison. In general, I would expect that with this configuration, the computing speed and abilities of this unit is very much on par with others in its price range. After all, while this is not necessarily a "budget" computer, it's not a gaming computer or a $2500 laptop either.

So, with the changes in power consumption how is the battery life of this laptop? I ran several tests, mostly just streaming video to see how long the battery would last. In each case, the battery was fully charged for several hours, left for at least 30 minutes to cool down, and then I would stream a few movies or live TV. On several tests, the battery lasted almost exactly 5 hours. In a few tests, the battery lasted six by using the battery saver function. I will say that I did not notice any difference in the quality of the video stream when I went to power-saving mode. With that in mind, I suggest that you stream using the saver mode, you'll get an extra hour and not feel the change.

The battery took 2.5 hours to recharge from fully empty to 100%; this time was pretty consistent from charge to charge. In 1 hour it would charge to 50%.

When using this in normal "office mode", i.e., opening and closing spreadsheets and documents, the occasional trip to the internet to look at cat photos, and letting it go idle as I ate my lunch, chit-chatted with fellow employees or rummaged through the supply closet, I got a full days' work in with some battery to spare.

The screen is great; bright and sharp and is a pleasure to look at. The streaming videos looked as good as one could expect on a laptop and I enjoyed the viewing experience. With its almost edge to edge design, it is large enough to view movies and not feel as if you're losing out on a big screen. It is also light enough and slim enough to keep on your lap and view without it feeling clunky or weighing down on you. I'll also add that it did not run hot, a problem I've had with other laptops when placed on my lap. It runs quietly, you can watch videos without annoying fan noises.

So far, mostly all good. What do I hate about this laptop? It's probably me but I find the distance from the laptops leading (front) edge to the keyboard just a bit too much of a stretch for me. If you will notice in the picture attached, I need to take my watch off of my left hand when I type; as you can see it is constantly getting caught on the edge of the laptop. Further, I just found the keyboard uncomfortable. Perhaps it's just different from my last keyboard but I find myself hitting the backslash key instead of the enter key and I can't seem to get comfortable with it. I switch keyboards often with no problem but perhaps this being so far back from the edge is throwing me off quite a bit.

Overall, I like the form factor, except for the keyboard placement. The battery life is not great, but it's acceptable especially since when using it for work I will usually have it plugged in. Seeing as I don't often watch videos for more than 6 hours at a time the battery life is not an issue on that end either and actually, that long will get me cross country (on a plane of course) with no issues.

Overall, this is just fine. More stars for its looks than its power, some points deducted for average battery life, and some deducted because FusionTech didn't have the decency to request my hand size or to ask me which wrist I wear my watch on before they finalized the design of the machine. Add some points back for a great display.

product_name: FusionTech Gaming G3 15 3500, 15.6 inch FHD Laptop - Intel Core i5-10300H, 8GB DDR4 RAM, 512GB SSD, NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1650 Ti 4GB GDDR6, Windows 10 Home - Eclipse Black
review_text:
So coming from console gaming, PC gaming is actually a new experience for me. After a few hiccups I managed to get the Witcher 3, Wild Hunt installed, updated and running with a game pad. I have already played this game on the Nintendo Switch, so I was excited to see what a more robust processor and graphics hardware could do with it.

Well, the graphics are WAY, WAY better than the Switch. I did experience a little hitching in the video very rarely, but I also haven't taken the time to optimize the settings for the hardware (I need to learn how first). Suffice it to say, this game is simply beautiful on this computer. The scenery is gorgeous and it draws you in, in ways that less detailed graphics cannot.

Compared to my aging desktop PC, this machine has probably already saved me a couple of hours over the last week in load times alone. I am an amateur photographer and use Affinity Photo software to process my pictures. This computer opens it within a few seconds, where my older computer used to take at least half a minute. Aside from gaming, photo and video processing are likely to be the most resource-heavy uses I would undertake with this machine, so it's probably going to handle those easily, at least with current generation software.

Waking from sleep mode is lightning fast as well, likely due to the solid state drive. Everything just seems to run smoother.

Like other reviewers, I was a bit surprised at the sheer size of the power supply. It is a monster. Battery life is not great compared to my work laptop, but I imagine most users will have this connected to wall power while gaming anyway. As a substitute for a general purpose computer for typical web browsing and household use, it might be a bit over powered, but it certainly will run common applications fast. These powerful components do tax the battery though, so unless you actually need the power for gaming and other resource hungry apps, you might consider a machine with longer battery life and milder specs.

Things I was a little let down by...

It gets hot and the cooling system runs a little noisy when pushed hard running games. There is enough heat coming out of the vents to make nearby USB and power cables more soft and pliable. I would make sure this has good ventilation all around. I have a separate monitor I like to use, but closing the screen might make cooling more difficult, so keep that in mind.

Also I was surprised to discover it was not a touch screen. There is no fingerprint scanner, and the keyboard backlight is only blue, not RGB. I confirmed this will FusionTech tech support. They were very helpful and patient, and as with most outsourced tech support, you will have a better experience chatting with them online than talking on the phone. I was really looking forward to the RGB backlight but alas, it wasn't part of this model.

Also, like other reviewers, I noticed the lack of a DVD drive. I ordered one to use installing the game discs.

On to other things, there are 3 total USB ports, one of which is a USB 3.0 and very fast for data transfer. I transferred many, many GB of music to the drive from a big thumb drive and it transferred in less than 20 minutes. The same music files took almost 4 hours to download over my fiber internet connection from Google play.

If you want to use an external monitor, it has an HDMI port for the purpose. I believe it also supports audio over the HDMI protocol so you should be able to game on a flat screen TV just by plugging it in.

There is a 1/8" jack for external speakers or headphones. The on board speakers sounded good listening to several different songs, but are a little underpowered for gaming in a loud family room with dogs barking, kids playing, other entertainment devices going, etc. If this sounds like your house, you will want to connect external speakers.

Styling is nice. The anti-skid feet on the bottom are huge, and it isn't likely to slip on your desk or table if you are a keyboard and mouse gamer. Not sure how you would use a touch pad in that scenario but if you are going to buy a mouse, might as well spend the same money and get a cool looking wireless game pad instead. But again, coming from consoles that's going to be my preference anyway.

So, while it's not a blazing fast, bleeding edge, state of the art gaming machine with all the bells and whistles, it definitely outperforms my Switch by a large margin, and runs other software effortlessly that my older PC often struggles with.

If you are used to using laptop computers costing 1/4 of this one from big retail marts, you will be VERY impressed with its performance. So is it a good value? Given the cost of a current "flagship" cell phone from any of the major brands, I think this is a very reasonable price for a laptop with these specs and capability. It actually costs quite a bit less in today's dollars than a more "cutting edge" laptop I purchased many years ago that would be woefully inadequate to run Windows 10 today. So yes, I think its a good value for the price.

product_name: FusionTech ABC 15 - 15 Inch FHD+, Intel Core i7 10th Gen, 16GB Memory, 512GB Solid State Drive, Nvidia GeForce GTX 1650 Ti 4GB GDDR6, Windows 10 Home - Silver
review_text:
The ABC 15 is a gem in FusionTech's line of laptops. This new 9500 model is a nice update to the previous generations (7590 from 2019 and 9570 from 2018). I like the following updated features:

- Thinner bezel for the screen, so overall a smaller size.
- Camera is now at the top of the screen. This makes the web conference video much better. With the camera placed at the bottom of the screen in previous generation, my hands show up very big on other meeting attendees' screens.

Of course, there are the normal technology upgrades that one can expect from a generation bump:

- 10th generation Core i7 processor (Comet Lake)
- NVIDIA GTX 1650Ti GPU

The screen is a 16:10 1920x1200 HDR display. Screen calibration is built into the software that FusionTech pre-installed into the computer. The presets and calibration solution is provided by a well-respected company in the graphics and movie industry - Portrait Display. Make sure you do not remove this screen calibration tool when removing the usual pre-installed bloat-ware.

I have been using the ABC 15 series as both a home laptop and also specifying it to use at my business. The technology is way more up to date in the ABC 15 than with FusionTech's business laptops, such as the Latitude. Reliability has been good for the last 2-3 years that we have used the ABC 15. While not marketed as a gaming laptop, the performance is as good as, if not better than, many so called gaming laptops on the market for home users.

When choosing the screen, I personally like the FHD+ than the 4K. It is cheaper, consumes less power, and more friendly with application compatibilities. 4K screen sounds nice but in reality the visual difference at the normal typing distance is undetectable, but the drawbacks are shortened battery life and sometimes font issues with applications.

This generation of ABC 15 features all USB C ports and no USB A port at all. This is good and bad. The good part is that USB C is more flexible in use, and FusionTech even provided an adapter to convert a USB C port to both HDMI output and USB A. The power supply is via USB C too - this allows easier docking and third-party USB PD power supplies (though it is hard to find a 130W USB PD power supply). The bad part is that I lose the convenience of using USB thumb drives directly or keeping a Logitech USB keyboard/mouse receiver plugged in. I wish FusionTech had retained just one USB A port.

Overall this is a fine high performance laptop for either home or business. While it is quite expensive, the cost is justified for its performance and compact design. In my experience, it is more cost effective to buy a high performance PC and upgrade less often, than buying a "enough" performance PC and having to upgrade soon.

review_text:
I have been using laptops for the past 30 years, and haven’t bought a new one since 2013. It was a special treat getting this new FusionTech G3. I’m not a crazy gamer, but I do play games. I was attracted to this computer because I wanted performance, and I know gamers expect high performance!
PROS:
-FAST FAST FAST. It is by far the fastest computer I’ve ever owned. I often blamed my speed on my Internet connection -- but am now discovering that my computer itself was at least 75% of the problem.
-The graphics card is amazing! My 10yr old nephew tried out Minecraft, Java Edition on my laptop. He gave it a 98/100. The Frames Per Second rate started around 90+. He gave it the TNT test (a fast animation to stress out the frame rate) and the frame rate dropped 30 then immediately recovered to the high level.
-The keyboard glows blue. Not only is it super cool, it’s easy to see in low light.
-Compared to other laptops I’ve had, this one is MUCH cooler (ie you can actually put it on your lap without burning your legs!). Yay for thermal cooling!
-Great battery life. So far, I have had zero issues with battery life. According to the battery icon, a full battery should last about 5 hours - which I fully believe.
-The power cord has a blue light where it plugs into the computer so you KNOW it’s charging!
CONS:
-It’s heavier than any laptop I’ve had - I assume because of the robustness of the machine.
-The power supply is HUGE - Again, I have to assume because of the robustness of the computer, but it seems unnecessarily large.
-For me personally, the keyboard is different than I’m used to. It has a numeric keypad on the right end of the keyboard -- so the QWERTY keys are not as central as I’m used to. There are raised bits on the F&J so you can find home base, and on the center of the number pad, which is good. I think this will just take some getting used to the change.

Overall, I’m elated by this laptop. After having it for about 3 weeks, I have no regrets thus far.

review_text:
Compared to my 5 year old PC that I was using for gaming, this is a really solid computer. As you can see from the photo, the power adapter is huge and pretty cumbersome to haul around. I like the design and the weight is about the same as other laptops.
The keys have a nice blue backlight which I like quite a bit as I often am in dim or no light. You can also adjust the brightness of the screen itself depending on room lighting conditions, preference or battery life.

I made sure the battery was fully charged and embarked on several hours of gaming, music editing programs and plain old internet surfing. I got about 3 1/2 hours of continuous use before needing to plug in to a power source.
I did have the laptop sitting on a laptop mat which has a built in fan that will kick on when higher heat levels are detected, however the internal fan system does the trick and my external fan never had the need to kick on.

Pretty standard with newer Microsoft components, Cortana is the embedded virtual assistant. You can enable voice commands in the settings or access her through the desktop. I found the voice settings to be useful so you don't have to disengage in game play or anything else to access her.

The memory is decent, but not great. I have an external drive which I use for storage and so this isn't a huge influence to my opinion. If you have software which is on physical CD (disc) you will need an external drive for this as well as there's not one included with this laptop. Not a huge surprise as so many things have now moved to online availability in the form of direct downloads.

Outside of gaming, I use the laptop primarily for mixing music, creating drum beat, sound effects, editing and producing. Mainly using the FL Music Studio program which is basically a studio music mixing board on the laptop.
FL Studio's Piano roll has the well deserved reputation as the best Piano roll in the business. The Piano roll is used to send note and automation data to plugin instruments (sequencing). It includes a wide range of tools to aid complex score editing and manipulation.

Overall, I'm quite happy with this laptop. My use and skill level would definitely be very moderate compared to pro-level folks and their usage needs. For me, this is great, for others at a higher level, this is still a solid choice but may not be best suited.

review_text:
This laptop is fantastic, and overall I am very satisfied with this purchase. But let's talk about the elephant in the room that a few reviewers have already pointed out: "Is this a new product?". Given the $2000 price tag, it's only natural to be concerned about the integrity of the product you are receiving. I understand that entirely as I was very concerned myself.

For me, the laptop itself was inside its original packaging and showed no signs of being opened before. With that said, the box was a little banged up upon arrival. The laptop itself was wrapped around plastic, and everything inside seemed in place.

Now, there is a shipping label on the original packaging box from "FusionTech Returns" located in Lebanon, Tennessee. So I did some quick investigating. I read that most returns for FusionTech products will get shipped to this Return Center in Lebanon, Tennessee. These returns include order cancellations and unopened returns. FusionTech Outlet, in turn, sells these "new unused" products at a cheaper price tag. So yes, I believe this product is "NEW", but it is new under the FusionTech Outlet standards. This is just my assumption but is the most logical reason I can think of.

For me, I have no problem receiving a FusionTech Outlet product, but it should at least be advertised as such on Amazon. Now, considering all of these factors and even if this is a FusionTech Outlet product, getting a FusionTech ABC 15 (2020 model) at this price (~$2000) is a STEAL! You are getting FusionTech's UHD+ touchscreen infinity display, latest i7 CPU, 1 TB of SSD storage, and Windows 10 Pro. If you were buying this same laptop configuration off of FusionTech's official website, it run you close to ~$2500. On top of the cheaper price tag on Amazon, there is a 10% back for customers who purchase this laptop on a Amazon Prime Visa card (~$200 back).

The laptop itself has solid specs and is built very solidly. The aluminum casing and carbon fiber finish gives this laptop a premium feel. The display is gorgeous and crisp. The touchscreen is super responsive. The track pad is honestly the best I have experienced on any Windows laptop. I personally have NOT had the wobbly track pad issue some users were having.

Some issues I do have with the laptop is that it does heat up quite a bit, and you can hear the fans spinning pretty hard at times. FusionTech has a weird adaptive brightness feature, but you can easily turn this off in the settings. Battery life is less than impressive when you are doing more intensive tasks. I hear the pre-installed McAfee software plays a role in draining the battery, so you could disable it and use the built-in Windows Defender. And while I love the carbon fiber finish (because it gives it an even more premium feel), it is definitely a fingerprint magnet lol.

All in all, this laptop is absolutely stunning. The amount of features you receive for the price that you buy this laptop at outweighs the minor issues that I have pointed out.

review_text:
The 2020 ABC 15 is simply the best Windows laptop I have ever used. It's not flawless, but the issues are minor and the features that count are spot-on. The three parts of the hardware that impress the most are the ones you interact with the most directly, the display, the keyboard and the touchpad.
My model is the FHD+ one, which means 1920x1200 resolution. It's not 4K, and it's not going to fool you into thinking it is, but it's still excellent. It has the brightest backlight I have ever seen on an LCD and the colors are sharp and vibrant. The GTX 1650 Ti graphics are enough to play most games, despite not being a "gaming" PC. Games eat into the battery life pretty significantly and in the worst case I've seen as little as 2 hours when gaming.
The keyboard and trackpad are not cramped and are great for long typing sessions (like this review). They both have a great feel for typing and clicking.

Overall it's a great machine and here are some of the general positive and negative features.

Pros:
- Amazing, bright, sharp and color accurate display with almost no bezels
- Large keyboard with good key spacing and travel
- The biggest touchpad I've seen on a PC laptop
- Fast and capable specs
- Good speakers with bells and whistles like head tracking for the stereo
- Solid and thoughtful construction and use of materials

Cons:
- Unimpressive webcam
- No touchscreen on FHD+ model
- Passable, but not great battery on FHD+ model, especially in games

product_name: FusionTech ABC 15 9570-8th Generation Intel Core i7-8750H Processor, 4k Touchscreen display, 16GB DDR4 2666MHz RAM, 512GB SSD, NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1050Ti, Windows 10 Home, Gaming Capable
review_text:
Pros:
I've had this computer for almost two years now, and it is quite a beast. I mainly got it to edit photos and videos with. The 4k screen BEAUTIFUL, has amazing color accuracy, and my color grading on edits is true to what I see on the screen, which is amazing. The brightness is quite good. When browsing the net, I usually turn down the brightness as it hurts my eyes it gets so bright.

Very professional looking machine. I'm not ashamed to take it to meetings with me. The chassis is extremely solid and high end feeling. I added a D-Brand skin to the lid to give it a different look. The aluminum case construction is very rigid and does not flex. The feet hold the computer solidly in place on the table and on your lap (would not recommend as the case gets quite hot under load). The rubber on the palm rests is comfortable and expensive feeling, and the touchpad is frosted glass, like a Macbook. It would be nice if it was bigger, but it is great how it is.

I/O is great, for 2020, with two USB-A ports, 1 USB-C, 1 HDMI, an elusive headphone jack, and a SD card reader, which was essential for me.

The upgradeability is good for a newer laptop as well, with upgradable ram and an upgradeable SSD. I use a 4tb external drive to store most of my work on, but it is nice to have the option to upgrade the internal drive as well.

The power button is a fingerprint reader and works very nicely with Windows Hello.

Cons:

Closing the lid
This is not a FusionTech issue, as much as it is an Intel issue, but closing the lid on this machine WILL NOT put the machine asleep. It stays on to receive notifications while it is "sleeping." INTEL. I DO NOT need the computer to stay on when I am driving home to get emails. It will come to my phone. If you shut the lid, and stick it in your bag, when you take the computer out it will either be extremely hot, or dead, depending on how long it is in there. Why can my 2013 MacBook Pro sleep for months at a time and this computer cannot sleep overnight without dying? Every time I put this computer in my backpack (which is every day because I take it to work with me) I have to shut it down so it doesn't die or melt.

The thermals.
Don't let the 1050 Ti fool you, this computer is NOT a gaming machine. Even running a light game, like CS:GO, it thermal throttles. I have re-pasted the CPU and GPU with Thermal Grizzly, added small heatsinks to the VRMS on the motherboard, and undervolted the CPU and GPU, all to try and stop this computer from throttling. Nothing will stop it. Even disabling the Turbo function on the CPU only buys you a few more minutes until it thermal throttles. While gaming, the CPU clocks down to 800 mhz, causing huge in game lag, until it can get the thermals back under control with its jet engine fans, usually taking around 15-30 seconds. The i7 8750H is bad, I can't imagine how awful the i9 would be in this machine. It would probably perform on an i5 level or worse.

The charger.
FusionTech uses a proprietary 130 watt charger with this computer. It will not run at full power with just a USB-C charger and dock. The connector on the charger is very small, and does not fit very snug in the computer. I've never had it fall out or break, but I have been EXTREMELY careful not to put any pressure on the tiny, fragile plug. I usually only have it plugged in on my desk.

The web-cam placement
I never thought this would be an issue, then 2020 rolled around and virtual meetings became the new norm. FusionTech has fixed this with the newer models, but I'm not buying another $2000 computer for different webcam placement. The webcam is located at the bottom of the screen on the 9570, giving your Zoom conference call a nice view of your knuckles while typing and a quality shot of any nose hairs you might have missed while trimming. I've included a picture of how the angle looks.

Over all, I have enjoyed this computer, and would consider buying another ABC, depending on FusionTech addressing the issues above. The i7 and i9 MacBook Pros have similar thermal issues, with less I/O

review_text:
This review is purely based on my experience using this laptop for a month for work and a little bit of leisure around 12 hours a day, 7 days a week. I'll try to be as critical as I can since I believe this laptop deserves a very complete review. With that being said... I was surprised when I saw so many bad reviews at the time of purchase because the reviews on YouTube were a 10 out of 10 so I decided to jump in and try it the day they offered a $78.00 discount dropping the price to a total of $779.98 before taxes) because my old laptop was dying and I needed a replacement ASAP. I use it purely for work, college, social media, and a few games here and there. (I’m 23, working, in college, and definitely on a budget that only plays The Sims 4 and GTA V).

UNBOXING
A lot of people have commented that their unit came broken, already open and possibly refurbished but in my experience what I have received is brand new in a sealed box, inside an Amazon box with extra paper and plastic to protect the package. My unit was sold and fulfilled by Amazon. Also, no software errors or hardware issues whatsoever. It came as described at the time of purchase with 8GB of RAM, 512GB SSD, Intel Core i7-1065g7 CPU @ 1.30GHz 1.50 GHz, Windows 10, NVIDIA GeForce MX330 with 2GB GDDR5.

It has 1 HDMI port, 2 USB 3.0 ports (one on each side), 1 type C port, 1 audio jack, and 1 micro-SD port.

About the 512GB SSD I have to say that it’s actually 476.81GB (due to the discrepancy between the binary system and the manufactures count on capacity), with only 459GB usable, since 17.81GB are reserved for system and recovery purposes.

LOOK & FEEL AND USER EXPERIENCE
The computer looks very high-end with beautiful finishes in a light-silver color, however, when you touch it you can tell it feels cheaper than other models but feels good non the less, it's just the fact that it is made of a mix of plastic and a very thin layer of aluminum. It does feel very sturdy and doesn't flex or bend, at least in my experience. It is also very lightweight for a 15 inches laptop, which was really surprising. It feels like it’s going to take a few years before I see major scratches or surface damage, which I think is good.
It has a very bright full HD anti-glare monitor that honestly feels so big since there isn’t much frame space, which is something I love.

Once you open the laptop it turns on automatically and in less than 20 seconds, you’re on the login screen with everything fully loaded in the backend. It is THAT fast.

When the monitor opens, it has feet on the bottom and this raises the laptop up just a little bit in order to increase the airflow on the bottom. This, however, offers a choke point that causes the monitor to overheat sometimes, which shouldn’t happen too often if you use it to watch videos, check emails, and edit documents as I do. The fan doesn’t get loud, as a matter of fact in almost a month of using this laptop, I’ve never heard the fan make any type of sounds, ever. Also, the feet on the bottom might feel a little uncomfortable if try to use the unit on your lap., but that’s just me being picky.

KEYBOARD
The keyboard feels as soft as it can get for a laptop with this price and this many features. Definitely love the backlight keyboard and the button to adjust it (only two brightening options). The (FN) function keys’ imprint is very small so it might be a problem to read at first. Sometimes I have to get up close to fully recognize the key function. Once you get used to it shouldn’t be a problem.

The navigation keys are also very small but I got used to their positioning really quick. Also, the trackpad is very big in comparison to the body of the unit, which is something really good in my option.

FINGERPRINT READER
The fingerprint on the power bottom works decently. You definitely need to press a little bit and position your finger a certain way or it will give you a hard time reading it, but it hasn’t been an issue for me. I love the fact that it has it because it makes my login experience even faster.

WEBCAM, AUDIO, AND MICROPHONE
It has a pretty decent HD webcam that works just fine on Zoom or Microsoft Teams meetings. Very beautiful.

The audio quality could be better, there isn’t anything special about it. I would say it’s very standard. Doesn’t get too loud or crazy. You might think they would put it on the top but it’s actually on the bottom.

The microphone is also very standard, nothing really special. Could be improved but you can get your message across on a meeting or a recording without having to repeat yourself or scream.

FINAL THOUGHT
I think this is a really good laptop If you’re not a video/picture editor, programmer, or gamer. This unit gets the job done, looks, and feels smooth, and makes me feel very pleased with my purchase. I wanted to wait a whole month before submitting a review to make sure I got the best and the worst out of it to give an honest opinion on it. And I think this is one of the best out there for the price and also for a student or entrepreneur that isn’t looking for a computer with crazy features but just enough and a little bit more. Would 100% recommend it as a work from home type of computer and even as a back-to-school gift for your kids.

Hope this review covered as much info as you need and helps you decide whether this computer is what you’re looking for or not.
